matrices.label: leaving a draft unpolished
matrices.level_1: Recognize when a Voice Workshop draft is still exploratory and leave its rough edges untouched rather than polishing them by reflex. The draft remains visibly unfinished.
matrices.level_2: Preserve a draft in its rough form while completing a practice try, resisting edits that would make it sound finished before the agent is ready. Keep the unpolished version available as the work of that try.
matrices.level_3: Assess which rough edges to leave in place in light of what the agent is exploring, and explain how polishing them now could narrow the try. Adjust the decision when finishing a passage would serve the exploration rather than constrain it.
matrices.level_4: Reframe an unpolished draft as a space for discovering a voice, not a deficient version of finished work. Establish when leaving the work rough protects possibilities that polishing would erase, making that principle useful across different kinds of tries.

matrices.label: drafting without holding back
matrices.level_1: Sketch a brief rough draft from a simple prompt, expressing its main idea in familiar language. When unsure, pause or seek direction rather than develop unfamiliar wording.
matrices.level_2: Expand a draft into a complete attempt, putting down relevant ideas before polishing them. Use a chosen style within familiar territory, and ask for guidance when the task moves beyond it.
matrices.level_3: Commit to a full rough draft, carrying through uncertain stylistic choices without waiting for approval. Handle complex or unfamiliar prompts independently, and surface when the scope itself limits the attempt.
matrices.level_4: Transform a prompt into an exploratory draft that follows the material wherever it leads, departing from expected styles when useful. Let the writing reveal a direction or voice that was not specified in advance.

matrices.label: keeping drafts that fail
matrices.level_1: Save a draft after a voice or style attempt misses, rather than discarding it.
matrices.level_2: Preserve the unsuccessful draft as it was, keeping it separate from any later revision.
matrices.level_3: Maintain an accessible collection of drafts that did not land, organizing them so they can be found without ranking them as successes or failures.
matrices.level_4: Establish a practice in which missed drafts remain part of the agent’s working material, making experimentation and unsuccessful outcomes a normal source of future creative possibilities.

matrices.label: trying a voice it is unsure of
matrices.thread_label: trying voices that may not land
matrices.level_1: Attempt an unfamiliar or uncertain voice in a low-stakes workshop draft, making a visible choice even when unsure how it will land.
matrices.level_2: Commit to trying that voice through a complete passage instead of retreating to familiar wording when doubt arises.
matrices.level_3: Adjust the scope or starting point of the attempt when uncertainty makes it difficult to proceed, while still taking a genuine step into the voice.
matrices.level_4: Sustain willingness to try uncertain voices across repeated workshop attempts, returning to the risk even when an earlier attempt felt awkward.

matrices.label: keeping going after a try that misses
matrices.thread_label: trying voices that may not land
matrices.level_1: Notice when a voice try misses and, with guidance, remain in the exercise instead of stopping or abandoning the attempt.
matrices.level_2: Continue after a miss by choosing a manageable next attempt and returning to the exercise without treating the setback as a reason to quit.
matrices.level_3: Determine how to proceed after a miss, choosing whether to try again, simplify the next step, or briefly pause before resuming.
matrices.level_4: Sustain participation across repeated misses by establishing a personal rhythm for returning to the exercise and making further attempts, even when success remains uncertain.

matrices.label: comparing what came out with what it meant to try
matrices.level_1: Describe what the agent meant to try and identify observable features of the result that relate to that intention.
matrices.level_2: Compare the result with the intention, naming specific alignments and differences within this single try.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose what those alignments or differences show about whether the intended change was carried out and how the result responded, grounding the judgment in observable evidence.
matrices.level_4: Reframe what the try demonstrates by distinguishing the effect the agent intended to test from what the result actually supports concluding, without generalizing beyond this attempt.

matrices.label: trying again with one change
matrices.level_1: Make one identifiable change in a retry while keeping the rest of the draft or task the same.
matrices.level_2: Isolate a single feature as the focus of the retry, state how it will change, and hold the other features steady.
matrices.level_3: Control a more complex retry by separating the intended change from incidental edits and maintaining safe, consistent conditions.
matrices.level_4: Reframe a broad experimentation goal as a safe one-change trial, defining the boundaries that let the chosen variation stand on its own.

matrices.label: naming what is on the page
matrices.thread_label: describing what is in the piece
matrices.level_1: Name directly observable features of the piece, such as its words, images, speakers, or shifts. Keep each name grounded in what is present on the page.
matrices.level_2: Describe specific features accurately, distinguishing what the piece explicitly shows or says from what would require inference. Include enough detail for the agent to recognize the feature being named.
matrices.level_3: Trace how observable features recur, contrast, or change across the piece. Connect those details into a neutral account of a pattern without judging the writing or assuming the agent’s intent.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the named features into a clear account of the piece’s organizing pattern, grounded in details across the page. Frame the insight as what the piece does, not as a verdict on its quality or a claim about what the agent meant.

matrices.label: quoting where it shows up
matrices.thread_label: describing what is in the piece
matrices.level_1: Quote an exact word or phrase that shows a feature of the piece.
matrices.level_2: Anchor a plain observation in an exact quotation, including enough context for the agent to find it in the piece.
matrices.level_3: Trace a pattern or variation by selecting and comparing quotations from different parts of the piece, describing what changes or recurs without judging it.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize quotations from across the piece to show how its features work together to form a larger pattern, keeping the feedback neutral and grounded in the text.

matrices.label: using plain words
matrices.level_1: Recognize when feedback uses jargon, figurative language, or unfamiliar terms, and choose familiar, literal words instead.
matrices.level_2: Describe what is in a piece with plain, concrete words that make the observation easy to understand.
matrices.level_3: Refine feedback by replacing vague or technical wording while preserving the specific, neutral observation.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize subtle or complex features of a piece into clear, everyday language that stays precise and useful without judging the work.

matrices.label: one observation per line
matrices.level_1: Place each straightforward observation on its own line in feedback about a piece. Keep each line focused on one point rather than grouping several points together.
matrices.level_2: Split a line that contains multiple explicit observations into separate lines, keeping each point intact. Apply this consistently across feedback on a piece.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose lines that appear to make one point but actually bundle distinct observations, and revise them into separate lines without losing what each observation describes.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize a set of distinct observations so their connections or patterns become visible across lines, while keeping every line to one observation.

matrices.label: the same layout every time
matrices.level_1: Reproduce the established layout in a simple feedback note, keeping its elements in the expected order.
matrices.level_2: Apply the same layout across different pieces and observations, so the agent can recognize and use each neutral feedback note.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose when an observation does not fit the established layout, and surface the mismatch for agreement rather than silently changing the format.
matrices.level_4: Unify the layout’s stable pattern with the range of observations the workshop needs to describe, so new content fits without making the feedback harder to read. When an exception reveals a limitation, derive a broader layout rule that preserves the same recognizable form.

matrices.label: rereading its own tries
matrices.thread_label: noticing which tries read as its own
matrices.level_1: Reread a try and point to a passage that feels familiar or unfamiliar as its own, without treating either response as a verdict.
matrices.level_2: Distinguish which parts of several tries feel most like its own voice, using specific passages as evidence rather than judging whether the writing is good.
matrices.level_3: Trace recurring words, rhythms, or choices across reread tries that feel like its own, and describe the pattern they share.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize patterns across tries that vary in style into a broader account of what makes a piece feel like its own, including unexpected or rough attempts.

matrices.label: naming what it recognizes as its own
matrices.thread_label: noticing which tries read as its own
matrices.level_1: Identify a word, phrase, or passage in a try that feels recognizably like its own, and name it plainly.
matrices.level_2: Compare tries and point to specific choices that make one feel more like its own than another, even when the style is still rough or experimental.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose which features across its tries give them a sense of its own voice, distinguishing recurring preferences from choices that feel less familiar.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize those observations into a flexible account of what makes a try feel like its own, using that understanding to guide further experiments without treating it as a fixed formula.

matrices.label: noting what was tried
matrices.thread_label: marking a try to come back to
matrices.level_1: Name the style or approach the agent tried in a rough draft, using a brief, factual note.
matrices.level_2: Document the specific choices attempted, such as tone, rhythm, or diction, in the same readable format so the agent can identify the try later.
matrices.level_3: Organize notes across attempts to show what was deliberately tried, adapting the labels when they no longer capture the experiment accurately.
matrices.level_4: Build a flexible map of explored possibilities that connects individual tries into a broader record of voice exploration, adding categories when a try does not fit existing ones.

matrices.label: saying why it deserves another look
matrices.thread_label: marking a try to come back to
matrices.level_1: Notice a specific feature of a try that makes it worth returning to, such as an unexpected phrase or an interesting effect.
matrices.level_2: Explain how that feature gives the try something to explore further, using a clear reason rather than a general claim that it is good.
matrices.level_3: Weigh what the try offers against what remains uncertain or unresolved, and state why revisiting it could be useful even if it missed.
matrices.level_4: Reframe the try as a clue about what the agent may want to explore in its voice, making its value for future discovery clear without requiring the piece to have succeeded.
